Biology — Structure of Chromosomes, Cell Cycle and Cell Division

ICSE Class 10 Question Bank

Generated 2026-08-19

Sourced from the repository: Selina textbook review questions (with official answers cross-checked via knowledgeboat.com), CISCE's own 2024 Competency-Focused Practice Questions (with official answer key), 6 Specimen Question Papers (2017, 2019, 2022 Sem1, 2023, 2024, and a paper filed in the exam-papers folder as '2025.pdf' that is actually a duplicate of the 2025 Specimen paper — its title page confirms 'SPECIMEN QUESTION PAPER', so it is cited here as the Specimen 2025 paper, not a real exam), and 9 years of actual ICSE board exam papers (2017-2020, 2023-2026, plus the 2025 and 2026 Improvement papers). Board-exam and most specimen-paper questions have no official published answer key in the repository, so their answers below are labelled 'Model Answer' (written to the standard expected by the mark scheme, but not the official scheme itself); the CISCE Practice Questions answer key, the Selina review-question answers (verified via knowledgeboat.com), and a few specimen items are labelled 'Official Answer'. Supplementary questions pulled from knowledgeboat.com's Progress Check section, icsehelp.com, and oswal.io are tagged 'Website — <site>'. Every diagram-referencing question in this pass uses an 'image_placeholder' description instead of a real image; embedding images (including the 15 diagrams already sitting in assets/Biology/CellDivision/ from earlier work on this chapter) is being handled separately, out of band, and is not part of this pass.

F. Case Study Based Question

Q101. Cell division is a part of a long series of events called the cell cycle. The cell cycle consists of two main phases – interphase and the division phase. There are two types of cell divisions which occur in our body for growth, repair, replacement and gamete formation. Mitosis and meiosis mainly differ from each other with respect to the number of daughter cells produced, the number of chromosomes in the daughter cells and the purpose of division, etc.
(i) Both kinds of cell divisions start after the completion of interphase which includes G-1 phase, S-phase and G-2 phase. Interphase is the preparatory phase. Choose the correct statement from the options given below:
(a) Mitosis occurs in each and every cell of the human body.
(b) Chromatids split into two homologous chromosomes during prophase.
(c) Chromatin fibres become distinct and develop into chromosomes during prophase.
(d) RNA and histamines are the components of chromatin.

[1 mark(s)] Source: Book — Selina Concise Biology X, Review Questions F(i)

Q102. (ii) Interphase is the longest part of the cell cycle which lies between two successive cell divisions. Choose the incorrect statement from the options given below:
(a) Interphase is followed by karyokinesis and then cytokinesis at last.
(b) Synthesis of RNAs and proteins occurs actively in the first growth phase (G-1 phase).
(c) Interphase also occurs between equational and reductional division phases of meiosis.
(d) Replication or duplication of DNA occurs in the synthesis phase (S-phase).

[1 mark(s)] Source: Book — Selina Concise Biology X, Review Questions F(ii)

Q103. (iii) Daughter cells formed from one parent cell after the two phases of meiosis (equational and reductional) are:
(a) Identical and diploid
(b) Four daughter cells are produced with haploid chromosome number.
(c) Two daughter cells are produced with diploid chromosome number.
(d) Both (a) and (c)

[1 mark(s)] Source: Book — Selina Concise Biology X, Review Questions F(iii)
